title.narrative: QUALITY AND COMPLIANCE INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT IN SIERRA LEONE

description.narrative: In the post WTO globalised market place, specific concerns have been raised that developing countries are not deriving the potential benefits from globalization. While markets are made #open# and #free#, developing countries have to overcome many obstacles to reap the potential rewards. A key challenge facing developing countries is the lack of national capacity to comply with the WTO Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) and Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) agreement requirements, which are now global trade embedded market requirements. In order to meet this challenge, developing countries need significant technical assistance to establish a National Quality System (NQS) and develop institutional infrastructure related to Standards, Metrology, Testing, and Quality (SMTQ); in order to be an able partner in the global trade regime. Sierra Leone has been a member of WTO since 23 July 1995. However, the country does not dispose of a National Quality Policy; a well developed Competent Authority for fisheries to ensure the quality and safety of the exported fishery products which is one of the major exports of the country or basic capabilities for micro-biological and chemical testing of products and facilities for equipment calibration for ensuring the accuracy of measurement.
